title: Session restore
description: The sessions a reboot or crash took away (docs/session-restore.md): GET /v1/sessions/restorable, read by any paired device; POST /v1/sessions/restorable/restore and POST /v1/sessions/restorable/dismiss, which need a device that may send and an Idempotency-Key. A retry with the same key is answered with the first answer. Refusals are the flat `{error, message}`.

RestorableReason.description: Why nothing can be offered. `boot_unknown`: this machine cannot read its boot id, so it cannot tell a reboot from a daemon restart, and it records nothing.

RestorableSession.description: One conversation that was open before the machine last restarted, is not open now, and has been neither restored nor dismissed.

place.description: The place id of the directory (POST /v1/places/{id}/…).

title.description: The manual title when one was known, else the session's own; empty when it had none.

last_seen.description: Unix seconds: the last complete reading that recorded it open, at most sessions.restore_seen_age stale.

RestorableSessions.description: GET /v1/sessions/restorable. `available` false carries `reason` and no sessions. Sessions are the previous boot's, most recently seen first.

previous_boot_last_seen.description: Unix seconds: the last time the previous boot was seen at all. Absent when there is no previous boot on record.

RestoreSessionsRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/restorable/restore. At most sessions.restore_batch conversations; a longer list is refused whole with `restore_batch_too_large`.

RestoreCode.description: Why one conversation was not restored. `not_restorable`: it is not on offer (never recorded, already answered, open now, or no boot id). `place_unavailable`: its directory is no longer a place this machine can open. `conversation_not_found`: the assistant no longer lists it for that directory. `open_failed`: the terminal could not open it; `message` says why. `over_capacity`: other sessions were being opened; ask again.

RestoreResult.description: One named conversation's answer. `ok` carries the new terminal (`id`, `backend`, and `attach` for a detached tmux server); otherwise `code` and `message`.

RestoreSessionsAnswer.description: The answer to a restore: one result per distinct conversation named, in the order named.

DismissRestorableRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/restorable/dismiss. Without `conversations`, every conversation on offer is dismissed.

DismissRestorableAnswer.description: How many rows on offer this dismissed. Zero is an answer: they were already answered, or none were named that are on offer.
